title: Sanitize and enrich ingest proxy with deduplication and trace linking
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Introduce a lightweight ingest proxy service that normalizes incoming structured logs (ndjson/JSON), performs idempotent deduplication, attaches correlation/trace identifiers, and emits enriched events to our Kafka topics and direct Loki/ELK parquets. This reduces downstream parsing errors and improves traceability for latency/error dashboards.
background: We currently see brittle parsing across multiple consumers: heterogeneous log shapes from SDKs, duplicated events from retrying clients, and missing trace links when systems propagate different header names. Existing collectors (Fluent Bit, Vector) do transformation but we lack a centralized enrichment step that can: (1) normalize field names and types, (2) dedupe noisy bursts, and (3) attach canonical correlation_id/trace_id for dashboard joins. Several recent incidents have been traced to duplicated error reports and unjoinable traces during region failovers.
proposed_solution:
Build `log-enrich-proxy` as an add-on ingestion tier in front of existing forwarders. Responsibilities:
  - Accept NDJSON/JSON and detect content-type; support backpressure via HTTP/2 and Kafka producer with ACKs.
  - Apply a light schema normalization layer driven by a centralized schema registry (JSON Schema + optional Avro fallback).
  - Perform deterministic deduplication using a sliding window keyed by (tenant, event_fingerprint). Keep a Redis bloom filter + LRU with TTL for 5 minutes to avoid persistent storage costs.
  - Resolve correlation ids: check known headers (X-Request-Id, X-Correlation-ID, traceparent), fall back to generated correlation_id, and look up matching trace_id via the trace-linker microservice when present.
  - Emit enriched event to two sinks: a high-throughput Kafka topic (raw-enriched) for downstream consumers and a batched Parquet push for cold storage/ELK ingestion. Also support direct Loki push for line-based logs with Loki labels attached.
  - Expose rich metrics (ingest_lag_seconds, parse_errors_total, deduped_events_total, enrichment_failures_total) and tracing for the enrichment pipeline itself.
implementation_notes: Prefer Rust or Go for the proxy for low-latency and small memory overhead. Use existing Kafka client library standards and our internal schema registry. Deduplication: compute SHA1 of canonicalized JSON payload (sorted keys, normalized numbers/strings). Redis keys use CRC32(prefix) + tenant id to limit cardinality. Trace lookup calls must be rate-limited and cached per correlation_id to avoid thundering herd. Failure modes: if trace-linker fails, proxy should continue and emit a metric and retry asynchronously.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy `log-enrich-proxy` to staging behind a test route with synthetic traffic. 2) Canary on low-traffic tenant group (5% of production) with Kafka sink only. 3) Enable Loki direct sink for same canary group and validate dashboards. 4) Gradually expand to 50% then full rollout, verifying dedup rates and parsing error reductions at each step. 5) Switch older forwarders to send to proxy via DNS weight shift. Rollback via proxy toggle in control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing errors from upstream sources reduced by >= 80% for canary tenants (measured by parse_errors_total)
Deduplication prevents > 90% of immediate duplicate bursts (measured by deduped_events_total vs raw events)
Enrichment latency p95 < 120ms for the proxy (monitor ingest_lag_seconds)
Trace correlation completeness improves (fraction of error logs with trace_id increases by >= 50%)
No data loss in Kafka sink during 1 hour of 2x synthetic peak traffic (verify acks and end-to-end counts)
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboards: Enrichment Overview (throughput, p95 ingest latency, parse errors), Dedup Dashboard (duplicate ratio over time, TTL evictions), Trace Linking Health (cache hit rate, backend errors). Alerts: paging for enrichment_failure_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, parse_errors_total spike > 3x baseline, Kafka producer error rate > 0.5%.
performance_targets: Single proxy instance handles 50k events/sec with median CPU < 60% and p95 latency < 120ms. Redis memory usage should remain < 4GB per shard for 5-minute dedupe window at production traffic. Kafka payload sizes must be batched to target 1-2MB per produce call for throughput efficiency.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalization and fingerprinting, integration tests for end-to-end flow with a local Kafka + Loki stack, chaos testing for Redis and trace-linker unavailability, load test harness that replays historical 24h traffic scaled to 2x to validate throughput and p95. Add property tests to ensure canonicalization is deterministic across languages.
open_questions: What key rotation/TTL should we use for dedupe fingerprints beyond 5 minutes for longer batch windows?
Do we want to make trace-linker lookup synchronous or best-effort async for different SLAs?
Should schema registry enforce strict rejection for unknown fields or only warn and forward?
